title: Treating a Bartholin's cyst
what: There is a small gland at the entrance to the vagina. If its duct gets blocked, a cyst or abscess forms. The doctor opens it and makes sure it does not come back.
why: When a painful lump or abscess appears at the entrance to the vagina.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: If you are or could be pregnant
All your medicines, especially blood thinners
If you had a cyst before

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: In the morning, wash with warm water.

prepare.title: Numbing
prepare.text: Usually local numbing is used, sometimes short anesthesia. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If you have anesthesia, do not eat or drink for several hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

steps: You lie on the exam chair
The doctor cleans the skin with antiseptic
A small cut is made, and the fluid is let out
Sometimes a small catheter is placed or the edges are stitched so the duct stays open
feel: The numbing injection is a quick prick
After the procedure, it hurts and aches for a few days
after: Warm sitz baths, if your doctor advises them
No sex until it heals. Your doctor will tell you for how long
If a catheter was placed, it is removed at the clinic
red_flags: Severe pain and swelling that keep getting worse

faq.a: Sometimes, yes. That is why the doctor makes sure the duct stays open.
